page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance, reaching 34.85 GB/sec and 15.13 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core scaling and memory subsystem performance present notable tradeoffs. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark memory score are positioned in the lower tier, and memory bandwidth for large blocks is limited to 32.55 GB/sec for read operations and 20.39 GB/sec for write operations.

The c4n-highcpu-4 instance is suited for workloads that prioritize single-threaded CPU execution over high memory capacity or massive multi-core parallelization. Supported instruction set extensions include Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like lightweight machine learning inference, where it achieves 35.08 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local storage, it is a cost-efficient option for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight web serving, and microservices that do not require large memory footprints.
